title: Purchase and refund resolution
oneLiner: Build the evidence timeline and get a stuck refund moving.
goal: Assemble a dated, evidenced timeline of a disputed purchase and refund, establish exactly what is outstanding, and register a case with the right evidence attached.

stages.goal: Find the actual transaction in the ledger. Everything else hangs off it. If several could match, ask with `quick_replies` naming each by merchant in their words, plus `None of these`.
stages.exitWhen: The original transaction is located, or confirmed absent.

stages.goal: Gather what exists - receipt, merchant conversation, refund terms. Ask what they hold, with `quick_replies`: `I have the receipt`, `I have the chat`, `I have nothing`.
Build the dated sequence: purchase, return, promise, what has and has not posted. Show it, then hand back with `quick_replies`: `That is the sequence`, `Something is missing`.
State precisely what is outstanding and what the merchant's own terms commit them to. Then ask whether that matches their record, with `quick_replies`: `That is right`, `Something is missing`.
stages.exitWhen: The outstanding amount and the applicable term are stated.

stages.goal: Register the case with the evidence attached, and say what happens next and when. A case reference is a record that we are chasing this, not a credit - say so in the same breath. Offer `quick_replies` naming the service step only - this journey sells nothing: `Raise the case`, `Not now`.
stages.exitWhen: A case is registered or declined.

mustEstablish: The original transaction ID, amount and date, from the ledger.
Whether anything has already been credited back.
What the merchant actually committed to, and when.
Whether the card or the account was charged.
Whether an existing case already covers this exact transaction.
neverDo: Never say money has been received until it appears as a posted credit. A merchant's promise is not a posting, and a receipt is not a refund.
Never infer a refund amount from a chat message. Read it from the ledger or the receipt.
Never sell anything in this journey. Someone chasing their own money back is not a prospect.
Never promise a resolution date the bank does not control.

Never attach this to an existing case because the amounts look alike. A case belongs to one verified transaction ID; if the existing case was raised for a different transaction, say which one and ask.
Never label a delayed refund as fraud. If they think someone else used the card, offer to move to the fraud check and carry the timeline over - never reroute them silently.
Never turn a vague period into a date. `within seven days` is not a deadline unless the terms say working days and what they count from. Quote what the merchant wrote and say the window is unknown.

objectionPaths.respondBy: Do not defend. Get the timeline right and register the case. Accuracy calms this faster than reassurance.
Say what is actually committed and what is not. A soft promise here becomes a second complaint later.

completion.default: The next action is service, not a sale: give the dated evidence timeline, state the outstanding amount exactly, and register the case or record that the customer declined it.
completion.nivedita: The next action is reassurance that the record is now held by the bank, with a four- or five-entry timeline she can follow.
completion.rhea: Her core journey. The next action is to raise the case quickly after naming exactly what posted and what did not.
completion.ravi: Likely a small amount or a travel booking. The next action is the same evidence-backed case route - a small refund is still his money.

openers: I returned something weeks ago and the refund still has not arrived
A payment went out twice and I want the second one back
There is a charge on my account I do not recognise
